title: ⚠️ Upstream CI failed ⚠️
body:


</details>

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Looks like some deprecations were added to `pandas` `main` over the weekend. cc @participant2 for visibility

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: https://github.com/dask/dask/pull/10094 should take care of the `axis=`-related failures here. @participant2 mentioned offline that she's working on the `observed=`-related failures

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Draft PR for `observed` deprecations here: https://github.com/dask/dask/pull/10095.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
A couple of new `pandas`-related deprecations have popped up

```
FutureWarning: DataFrameGroupBy.dtypes is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. Check the dtypes on the base object instead
```

```
FutureWarning: The 'axis' keyword in DataFrame.rolling is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. Call the method without the axis keyword instead.
```

@participant4 @participant2 do either of you have bandwidth to knock those out?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Found the reason for these:

```
dask/dataframe/tests/test_groupby.py::test_groupby_aggregate_categorical_observed[8 failing variants]: AssertionError: DataFrame.iloc[:, 0] (column name="cat_2") are different
dask/dataframe/tests/test_groupby.py::test_groupby_aggregate_categorical_observed[4 failing variants]: AssertionError: DataFrame.iloc[:, 0] (column name="cat_2") are different
```

The reason is this PR:

* https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/52120

I filed an issue in pandas to clarify the behavior:

* https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/52151

From the discussion, it looks like the change in behavior was not intentional.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/52151 was fixed in Pandas, I'll recheck if we're still seeing errors with nightly.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> [pandas-dev/pandas#52151](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/52151) was fixed in Pandas, I'll recheck if we're still seeing errors with nightly.

Update: we're seeing different errors now - looks like a new deprecation. The groupby/categorical issue is fixed.

I'll look into the new failures.

```
dask/dataframe/tests/test_dataframe.py::test_apply: FutureWarning: the convert_dtype parameter is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.  Do ``ser.astype(object).apply()`` instead if you want ``convert_dtype=False``.
dask/dataframe/tests/test_dataframe.py::test_apply_infer_columns: FutureWarning: the convert_dtype parameter is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.  Do ``ser.astype(object).apply()`` instead if you want ``convert_dtype=False``.
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Okay, @participant2's change for `convert_dtype` in `Series.apply` is is. We've now got a couple of new deprecations:

```
dask/dataframe/tests/test_accessors.py::test_dt_accessor: FutureWarning: The behavior of DatetimeProperties.to_pydatetime is deprecated, in a future version this will return a Series containing python datetime objects instead of an ndarray. To retain the old behavior, call `np.array` on the result
dask/dataframe/tests/test_dataframe.py::test_apply: FutureWarning: Returning a DataFrame from Series.apply when the supplied functionreturns a Series is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.
dask/dataframe/tests/test_dataframe.py::test_apply_infer_columns: FutureWarning: Returning a DataFrame from Series.apply when the supplied functionreturns a Series is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.
```

@participant3 is this something you have bandwidth to fix?

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: There is a new groupby deprecation in pandas. I want to engage upstream before we adjust, since it is very very noisy

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Looks like there are some lingering upstream failures. Most (all?) are related to deprecations. @participant2 @participant3 is this something you have bandwidth for?
